# Code Smell Report

<!-- GENERATED by tools/coop/smell_report.py --write. Do not edit by hand. -->

Tracks the legacy hand-written TU smell families (extern "C" outside `lbl_*`, `self` free-function params, `void*`, raw pointer arithmetic, register-named params, inline asm, goto chains). New harness-produced code is already gated by `tools/pi_harness/lint.py`; this report makes the legacy backlog visible and prevents it from growing. **Goal: every number in this table trends to 0.** The curated pointer-arithmetic section below splits raw-offset sites by whether the enclosing function is already accepted, so the *actionable* backlog (raw offsets inside matched code) is explicit rather than buried in unmatched bodies.
The three `*shim`/`side-effect` rows are **fakematch-candidate** families: source shapes that reproduce retail *codegen* instead of retail *source* (`DECOMP_ASM_INSN` single-instruction asm blocks, `#pragma schedule` scheduling knobs, assignments inside casts in initializers). Each count is a candidate for the natural-rewrite hexdiff test, not a proven fakematch.

## Actionable pointer arithmetic (curated, per-expression)

The `ptr-arith`/`deref-arith` rows above are **line-based proxies**: a line carrying a cast plus an offset bumps `ptr-arith`, and the same line's deref independently bumps `deref-arith`, so one expression can move two counters. This section counts individual expressions with `tools/coop/detect_pointer_arithmetic.py` and splits every TU by whether the enclosing function is already accepted (`targets.json`). Sites inside accepted functions are the **actionable backlog** (typed field/pointer rewrites are byte-identical and `hexdiff`-verifiable now); sites in unmatched functions are a **churn budget** — those bodies get rewritten while matching, so cleaning them early is wasted work plus `-ipa file` line-shift risk. **Target: `ptr-acc` -> 0; `ptr-sites` follows as TUs reach acceptance.** These counts are informational and not part of the strict regression gate: acceptance migration moves existing sites into the accepted set, so the accepted total is not monotonic.

## TU-local view structs (debt audit)

A `struct XView` declared in a `.cpp` that types a raw offset into an object is an **interim** idiom, not an end state: it duplicates layout knowledge outside the owning class. `tools/coop/view_audit.py` resolves what each view wraps and classifies it - **opaque** (`u8*`/`void*`/temp buffer/call result), **vendored** (header under `nw4r/`, `revolution/`, `RVL_SDK/`, `CriWare/` - cannot be edited), **debt** (wraps a project class whose header declares no member at that offset), **duplicate** (the class ALREADY declares a member there - the view contradicts the header), **unconfirmed** (owner header has no offset comments), **reverted** (an attempt log records that the view was tested and kept - a view that cannot become a member without declaring a false one). Migrate a debt view with a **line-neutral in-place padding replacement** (`u8 pad_74[4];` -> `CFileHandle* mFileHandle;`): same line count, same offset, so no includer `-ipa` re-baseline is needed. Counts are informational (heuristic classification).

## Notes

- **extern "C" is name-table-mandated, not retail-mandated.** The US retail `main.dol` is stripped — `grep -a` finds no occurrence of `wkRender`, `__ct__cf_CfCamFollow`, `func_8004B0B0` or `lbl_eu_*` (the only `CDeviceGX` bytes are a `.rodata` class-name string), so retail carries no names to reproduce. Every name comes from `config/<region>/symbols.txt`, the dtk-built table that `dtk dol split` also uses to name the synthetic target objects; `extern "C"` only forces MWCC to emit that literal string. `extc.py`'s "retail-exact" therefore means only "this string is in our own table" (circular), and PLAN.md §17.6 classes these spellings as **legacy cleanup debt to retire**, not a floor. Three buckets, cheapest first:
  1. **data/array decls — free.** MWCC does not mangle namespace-scope variables, so `extern "C" u32 lbl_eu_x[];` and `extern u32 lbl_eu_x[];` emit the same symbol. A/B on `libs/monolib/src/math/FloatUtils.cpp`: 93 definition decls de-`extern "C"`ed **in place** (line-neutral — no `-ipa file` shift), `hexdiff --all` still 1/1 FULL_MATCH with a byte-identical reloc list and `run.py data diff` still MATCH (`.sdata2` 488 bytes identical).
  2. **hand-spelled mangled names** (`__ct__…`, `name__Class…`) are the rename shields — move the declaration to the owning header and `#include` it (SKILL "Declaration drift" path), keeping the edit line-neutral.
  3. **placeholder / short-form names** (`func_*`, `lbl_eu_*`, `__ct__CBgTex`) need symbol recovery: normal C++ mangles them differently, so keep `extern "C"` until the real class/member is known, then `symbols rename-plan` + `rename-all` (the one case that changes the emitted symbol).
- **`self` is legit when it is the ABI** (plugin callbacks: `VMThread* self`). It is a smell when a class already exists in a header and the function could be a member instead of an `extern "C" void* self` free function.
- `void*`→typed-pointer and pointer-arithmetic→struct-field refactors are **byte-identical** (types are erased at codegen) and the first cleanup to do; verify with `hexdiff` per function.
- Converting an extern "C" *function* into a real C++ member changes the emitted (mangled) symbol name, so it needs the `symbols rename-plan` + `symbols rename-all` + re-verification ceremony per TU — unlike the data/array case above, which is symbol-identical.
